name: Montana
agency: Montana Department of Justice, Motor Vehicle Division (MVD), Driver License Bureau
permitAge: 14 1/2 if enrolled in an approved traffic education course (secondary sources); otherwise sources conflict between 15 and 16

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night (75 with 15 at night if the online parent-taught course was used, per IIHS)
teen.nightLimit: First-year restricted license: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless an exception applies (MCA 61-5-133)
teen.passengerLimit: First 6 months: no more than one passenger under 18 unless supervised by a licensed driver 18 or older; secondary sources say up to three in the second 6 months; restrictions last 1 year or until 18
teen.phone: No statewide hand-held or texting ban (SB 359 failed in 2025); local bans in some cities and counties

notes: Exam figures (33 questions, 27 to pass) are from secondary practice-test sites only; not confirmed by MVD. Sites disagree on 80% vs 82%, so passPercent left null.
Official manual found hosted by the Office of Public Instruction (opi.mt.gov), referring to dojmt.gov/driving; no Spanish manual found. Spanish availability of the official test unknown.
Learner supervision under 18: parent/guardian, or with permission a licensed driver 18 or older (MCA 61-5-106).
Learner license valid one year (Montana Driver Manual).
Restricted license: every occupant belted, no more occupants than belts (MCA 61-5-133).

Speed (MCA 61-8-303, 2023): 80 mph rural interstate, 65 mph interstate in urbanized areas of 50,000+, 70 day / 65 night other highways, 25 mph urban district; may exceed by 10 mph while passing in a passing zone on two-lane roads. Daytime = 1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset.
Move over (HB 470, 2023, repealed 61-8-346): slow down and move to non-adjacent lane; reported figures (20 mph below on interstate, half the limit elsewhere) conflict, so questions stay general.
School bus: with a raised median only same-direction traffic stops (Montana Highway Patrol via STN); undivided roads all lanes stop.
Seat belts secondary for adults; primary for child under 6 and under 60 lb.
Open range (MCA 81-4-203): unfenced land including public highways; MSU Extension advises stopping and waiting for livestock.
